questions.text: Which description matches Whisper’s core encoder–decoder pipeline?

options.A: The encoder reads text tokens; the decoder generates waveform samples.
options.B: The encoder reads raw waveform samples; a CTC head labels each sample.
options.C: The encoder reads log-mel features; the decoder generates text tokens autoregressively.
options.D: The encoder reads speaker identities; the decoder generates image patches.

questions.explanation: Whisper encodes log-mel spectrogram features through a convolutional stem and transformer encoder, then generates text with an autoregressive decoder.

questions.text: A transcription application also needs to identify which speaker spoke each segment. What additional capability is needed beyond Whisper’s transcription and timestamps?

options.A: A speaker-diarization component that assigns speaker labels.
options.B: A larger text vocabulary that includes more punctuation tokens.
options.C: A causal mask that blocks all previous audio frames.
options.D: An output head that converts the transcript into a mel spectrogram.

questions.explanation: Whisper does not natively provide speaker diarization; assigning speaker labels requires an additional component.

questions.text:
What does whisper_prompt("fr", "translate", timestamps=False) return?

```python
def whisper_prompt(lang="en", task="transcribe", timestamps=True):
    tokens = ["<|startoftranscript|>", f"<|{lang}|>", f"<|{task}|>"]
    if not timestamps:
        tokens.append("<|notimestamps|>")
    return tokens
```
questions.explanation: The supplied language and task become prefix tokens, and timestamps=False appends the no-timestamps token.
